title: Global Media Distribution for Urban Transit Maps
business: A municipal transit authority providing real-time digital map updates to millions of commuters via mobile applications.
problem: The central origin server experiences high latency and connection timeouts during peak morning commute hours as global users simultaneously request large, static map tile assets.
solution: Amazon CloudFront acts as a content delivery network, caching map tiles at edge locations closer to the end-users. This offloads traffic from the origin server and serves content from the AWS edge network, ensuring that users receive map data from the nearest geographic point rather than the central server.
steps: Create a CloudFront distribution and configure the transit authority's origin server as the primary source for map tiles.
Define cache behaviors to specify how long map tiles should remain in the edge cache before re-validating with the origin.
Configure the distribution to use HTTPS for secure delivery of map assets to mobile clients.
Update the mobile application endpoints to point to the CloudFront domain name instead of the direct origin server URL.
outcome: Commuters experience faster map loading times and the transit authority's origin server maintains stability by serving only a fraction of the total requests.
limitation: Cache invalidation is not instantaneous; if map data is updated, users may see stale tiles until the Time-to-Live (TTL) expires or an explicit invalidation request is processed, which can be verified by checking the 'X-Cache' header in HTTP responses.
